title: Production Notification Service

requirements.businessGoal: Notify students automatically when their job application status changes, without duplicate or lost notifications.
functionalRequirements: Expose an internal API that accepts a status-change event for an application.
Deliver a notification to the affected student for each status change.
Prevent duplicate notifications for the same status-change event.
nonFunctionalRequirements: The service must remain correct under concurrent status-change events for the same application.
A failed delivery must not silently disappear — it must be retryable or visible in history as failed.
assumptions: Notification channel (email/SMS/push) is not specified and is left to the student to decide and justify.
ambiguities: Retry policy on delivery failure is unspecified.
Whether delivery is synchronous or asynchronous is unspecified.
constraints: Duplicate applications for the same job by the same student are already prohibited upstream — this service only handles the notification concern.
Unauthorized callers must not be able to trigger notifications for students they don't own.
edgeCases: Status changes twice in rapid succession before the first notification is delivered.
The same status-change event is submitted twice due to an upstream retry.
The student record no longer exists at delivery time.
acceptanceCriteriaSummary: A status change produces exactly one notification record, even under retries.
Notification history is queryable per student.

acceptanceCriteria.requirementRef: Expose an internal API that accepts a status-change event.
acceptanceCriteria.description: POST /events/status-change accepts a valid event and returns 202.

acceptanceCriteria.requirementRef: Deliver a notification to the affected student.
acceptanceCriteria.description: A single status-change event results in exactly one notification record.
acceptanceCriteria.expectedBehavior: notification_history has exactly 1 row for the event.

acceptanceCriteria.requirementRef: Prevent duplicate notifications for the same status-change event.
acceptanceCriteria.description: Submitting the identical event twice (simulated network retry) still produces exactly one notification.
acceptanceCriteria.expectedBehavior: notification_history has exactly 1 row after 2 identical submissions.

acceptanceCriteria.requirementRef: Unauthorized callers must not trigger notifications for students they don't own.
acceptanceCriteria.description: A caller without ownership of the student record is rejected.

acceptanceCriteria.requirementRef: The service must remain correct under concurrent status-change events.
acceptanceCriteria.description: Two rapid status-change events for the same application both result in correctly ordered, non-lost notifications.
acceptanceCriteria.expectedBehavior: notification_history reflects both events in correct order, no lost writes.

securityRequirements: Caller authorization must be verified server-side, not trusted from a client-supplied student_id.
No secrets or internal identifiers leaked in API error responses.
performanceRequirements: POST /events/status-change should respond in under 300ms under normal load, excluding actual delivery latency.
documentationRequirements: README explaining the chosen delivery model (sync/async), retry policy, and idempotency strategy, with reasoning.
